 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Brittany Mahomes was furious with the refs in last week's Kansas City Chiefs vs. Denver Broncos game.
 The wife of the Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback blasted the officiating crew for a false start penalty that wiped away a go-ahead touchdown. Brittany Mahomes felt that the officiating crew cost her husband's team the game. Denver topped Kansas City, 28-24, on Sunday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "You can't tell me you call that on a game winning TD," Brittany Mahomes, 31, wrote in a post to her Instagram Stories. "Oh wait yeah I can cause it's us."
 She continued, "That's the weakest call I have ever seen. You can't tell me otherwise."
 KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI – JANUARY 18: Brittany Mahomes on the sideline prior to the AFC Divisional playoff game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Houston Texans at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on January 18, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images)Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images
 The loss dropped the Chiefs to 5-2 on the season. Kansas City is no longer the favorite to win the AFC West.
 But was Mahomes right about the penalty call?
 Travis Kelce says no.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The three-time Super Bowl-winning tight end says that the referees got it right: It was a false start.
 Travis Kelce says Brittany Mahomes was wrong about penalty call
 During an episode of this week's "New Heights" podcast, Travis's brother, Jason Kelce, said: "A lot of people are saying this wasn't a penalty; I'm going to go on record and say that this is definitely a penalty."
 Travis agreed with his brother, replying: "Yeah, he flinches."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The three-time Super Bowl-winning tight end added that the Chiefs could have still won the game, too.
 "At the end of the day, we still had another play," Travis said. "I'll take my guy Pat Mahomes on the six-yard line with the game on the line.
 "I'll take that any day of the week. So we gotta execute at the end even more. We can't let the penalty absolutely deflate us and not let us execute at the end of the game."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Chiefs will look to rebound this week, taking on the Jets at 1 p.m. E.T. on CBS.
